en.title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Deleting One Character
en.description:
Delete exactly one character from a lowercase string and return the lexicographically smallest remaining string.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, solution, and tests.
en.output: Output the smallest string obtainable by deleting one character.
en.explanation:
Example 1: deleting c gives ab, which is smaller than ac and cb.

Example 2: the string is non-decreasing, so deleting the last t gives ho.

Example 3: deleting any a gives aaa.
hints: Delete the first character that is strictly greater than the character after it; if there is no such descent, delete the last character.
